searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's; the appellation search on winesofgreece.org counted with Alpha Estate. Four were restricted to a body's own domain (winesofgreece.org, karanika.com, amyntaswines.gr, visitwestmacedonia.gr) and read as primary for that body's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; a fact true of one vintage only was tied to that vintage.

tested: The founding in 1997 by a viticulturist and an oenologist after work in other Greek regions: the Greek travel trade directory, an American importer's shop page and a Greek profile site agree; kept, abroad cut.

The block of 1919, ungrafted bush vines on sand, about 650 metres, named after its former owner and bought from his descendants: a British merchant, an American drinks site and a Greek wine writer's pages agree (647 metres, gobelet); kept. One account dates the purchase to 2002, alone, so left undated.

Destemming, light crushing, cold soak and fermentation on yeasts isolated from the block: a British merchant and a wine writer agree; kept. Barrel time: 24 months in new Allier oak for the 2015 by one account; the record's range of eighteen months to two years in French oak kept, new oak left out.

Hedgehog, steel fermented and twelve months in French oak: a critic's note and an American merchant agree; kept. SMX, Syrah, Merlot and Xinomavro, PGI Florina: two critics' listings and the importer agree; the trap kept.
PDO Amyndeon from 1972, Xinomavro alone: Wines of Greece (search on its own domain); kept.
changed: story: the founders were said to have worked across Greece and abroad; now in other Greek wine regions, as the founding accounts read say, abroad cut for want of a source.
story: the estate vineyard was said to lie at over 600 metres; now about 600 to 700 metres, as the estate accounts give 580 to 710.
wine.label: Ecosystem was said to be carried on other reds of the range too, unsourced; now only that the house has printed it on this wine's label in some years.
open: The purchase of the Barba Yannis block is dated 2002 by one account only, so the story keeps it undated.
One importer calls the SMX blend, PGI Florina, the estate's flagship red; Barba Yannis stands as the pick because it is the appellation's own wine, and no swap is proposed.
The barrel time is a range across vintages; one account gives 24 months in new Allier oak for the 2015, so new oak stays out.

tested: The couple from the Netherlands who began in 2004: the house's Story and vision page (search on karanika.com) and two American merchants agree; kept. 2006 as the first vintage, one importer, still left out.

Seven villages, organic vineyards since 2009: the importer's producer page; Assyrtiko and Limniona beside Xinomavro: merchants; the gravity flow winery and cellars holding wines up to twelve years: the house's Winery page; kept.

The 2017 sheet: Rasto, Sotirtsko and Bella Toumba, 650 metres, ungrafted, hand picked on 12 and 13 September, basket pressed whole bunches, no sulphur, bottled January 2018, 54 to 84 months on the lees, six months after disgorgement: the house's sheet as the importer hosts it; kept. Fermentation in stainless steel and 20 hectolitre foudres by a second listing: changed.
The 2015 had about three years on its lees, a third in oak, by a wine writer: so the five to seven years is tied to the 2017.
The New York listing of 2016: searched for on the house's own domain and beyond, not found: cut.
changed: wine.making: the base wine was said to ferment in foudres alone; now in stainless steel and in foudres of twenty hectolitres, as the 2017 listing gives it; the five to seven years on the lees is now tied to the 2017, four and a half to seven years, since the 2015 had about three years.
story: the New York restaurant listing of 2016, found in no search of the house's own pages or elsewhere, cut.
story: the co-operative had tried sparkling wine since 1971; now first tried it in 1971, by the co-operative's own history and a second profile.
story: the closing claim that it is the reference for long aged sparkling Xinomavro, a judgement of rank, now a line on what long lees ageing teaches.
table: five years and more on its lees, true of the 2017 only; now years on its lees.
questions[1]: the option and explanation of 2016 rested on the cut New York listing; now 1971, the co-operative's first sparkling trials.
open: The label category Wine of Greece rests on a critic's tasting titles only; a bottle should be read.
The flagship has become Cuvée Céleste from the 2019 vintage; the read together agent may retitle the pick (see the review file).
Pear skin in the glass rests on a house note shared with another cuvée.

tested: The union of 1945, the winery of 1959, the first red of 1960, the sparkling trials of 1971: the house's History page (search on amyntaswines.gr) gives 1945 and twenty seven member co-operatives as a present count; a critic's profile gives 20 March 1946, the winery of 1959, the red released the following year and the trials of 1971; Greece and Grapes agrees on 1959. The founding year now the 1940s; the rest kept.

The appellation: Wines of Greece gives 1972 and lists dry rosé, dry red, sparkling dry and semi dry rosé, Xinomavro alone, and says rosé is significant in Amyndeon alone among the PDO zones; one secondary account says still dry rosé was added in 1995. The story no longer dates still rosé to 1972.
The ministry's product specification for PDO Amyntaio was found (minagric.gr) but could not be read through its summary.
changed: story: the union was said to be founded in 1945 by twenty seven village co-operatives; the house gives 1945, a second profile 20 March 1946, and twenty seven is the union's count of member co-operatives in its own day, not at its founding; now in the 1940s, with no count.

story: the appellation was said to cover red, rosé and sparkling wine from 1972 and Greece to have drawn up its first appellations then; Naoussa came in 1971, and one account dates still dry rosé to a later addition, so now 1972, a year after Naoussa, for red and sparkling rosé, the dry rosé covered since.
open: The year still dry rosé entered the appellation, 1995 in one account, is not told.
The house's claim to the only rosé PDO of Greece is told as its claim; Wines of Greece says only that rosé is significant in Amyndeon alone among the PDO zones.
The wine name in Latin letters was not seen on a bottle.

tested: The family wine trade before the Second World War and the restart of 2000 from an old family vineyard: found only in the same words on a critic's producer page and the merchant's page; a Greek local press piece covers the critic's notes on three wines of the house; hedged as the house's account.
7 Roots, Xinomavro alone, PDO Amynteo, 2021: two merchants agree; its making on one merchant's sheet, kept hedged.
Dodekatos, a blanc de noirs of Xinomavro, PGI Florina, wild yeasts, oak on fine lees: one Greek merchant; its existence as a blanc de noirs: two American merchants; kept.
changed: story: the family history was put to a Greek merchant's page; it is the account the house gives, printed in the same words by a merchant and a critic's producer page, so it is now hedged as the house's account.
story: the appellation was said to cover red, rosé and sparkling wine without qualification; now its rules allow Xinomavro alone, for red, rosé and sparkling rosé.
open: THIN: no page of the house was found; the family history rests on one origin, the house's own words as a merchant and a critic print them.
The sources' addresses carry the house's full trading name, which holds the living vintner's first name; the integrator should rule whether they stand.
The making of 7 Roots rests on one merchant's sheet; Dodekatos, its wild yeasts and PGI Florina on one merchant, its existence as a blanc de noirs on two more.

tested: The winery on the outskirts of Agios Panteleimon, among the four lakes, beside Lake Vegoritida on the slopes from Mount Voras, called Kaimaktsalan, and its visits: the regional tourism body and a tour operator agree; kept.

The Xinomavro 2019, PDO Amyndeon, twelve months in oak and twelve in bottle: the Wine Plus note alone; kept hedged. A wine writer's notes on the 2012 and 2013 show the wine made for a decade; not cited, the address carries a living name.
The founding, the owners, the house's own page: a Greek search found none; a Greek business press list of ten wines of Amyntaio names Vegoritis Xinomavro.
changed: story: growers were said to have sent their grapes for generations to the co-operative, unsourced, and Greece to have drawn up its first appellations in 1972; now the co-operative's winery opened in 1959 and the plateau became an appellation in 1972, a year after Naoussa.
story: the magazine note was dated to publication in 2024, unconfirmed; the year is cut.
open: THIN: no page of the house, no founding year and no owner were found; the place rests on the regional tourism body and a tour operator, the ageing on one magazine note.
Others holds a line saying no other wine was confirmed; the integrator may judge that line unfit to ship.
The regional tourism body files the winery in its Kozani unit list while both place accounts put it at Agios Panteleimon in Florina; the place line keeps Agios Panteleimon.

swaps.why: Not a swap of producer but a retitling the author raised. The vintages read (2016, 2017) carry the plan's name, the 2017 sheet is the record's primary source, and Cuvée Céleste from 2019 is told in others, the story, a trap and a card. The read together agent may retitle once a Céleste sheet is read; the key may then stay karanika.

The author proposed none. Vegoritis's place and its PDO Xinomavro rest on the regional tourism body, a tour operator and a magazine note, while no search showed Pavlou at work after about 2010; Vegoritis stands as a thin pick, told plainly as one.

codexTension: The region summary dates the appellation to 1972 and says it covers dry red, still rosé and sparkling rosé; one secondary account dates still rosé to an addition of 1995. Reported, not edited.
